newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Boeing, Airbus mull Israel Aircraft pact.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, Airbus mull Israel Aircraft pact.

text.p: State-owned Israel Aircraft Industries (IAI) is holding talks with Boeing Corp and Airbus Industrie about developing next-generation mid-air refueling aircraft, an IAI spokeswoman said on Sunday.
"The talks are at a very preliminary stage and no concrete proposal has been discussed," she said.
Israeli press reports said the two companies had separately approached IAI about development, production and sale of refueling aircraft, but the spokeswoman would not confirm any details.

Boeing has proposed using its 767 jet for a joint venture aircraft while Airbus is proposing its A-320, according to industry sources. Boeing produces refueling planes and Airbus is considering entering the field.
IAI's Bedeq Aviation Group is considered a world leader in the field and has sold dozens of planes to 10 countries, including Chile, Australia, Colombia and Venezuela.
